summary: Bhagavan Das was an Indian philosopher and Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He served as Honorary Secretary at Central Hindu College (~1899–1914) and headmaster at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1926).

Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indologist and linguist. His career includes posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1976), where he later served as head of the Research Department (attested 1989).

Bhagwan Dash was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He studied at ITRA, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi, where he completed an M.A. and a PhD (1978). He worked as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was an honorary member of the Royal Asiatic Society (1877), a Mumbai University Fellow (1882), and an Asiatic Society of Mumbai member (~1877–1888).

Bhajagobinda Ghosh worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1994, he held posts as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as an Editorial Board Member for the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi (master's), and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University (linguistics doctorate), later holding posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

Bhaskar Anand Saletore was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He studied under Henry Heras and completed his doctorate supervised by Lionel David Barnett. By 1936, he served as Professor of History at Sir Parashurambhau College.

Bhau Daji was an Indian scholar in the fields of Indology, history, and archaeology. He pursued his education at Elphinstone College and Grant Medical College and Sir Jamshedjee Jeejeebhoy Group of Hospitals (~1845–1850).

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Peradeniya and a Habilitation from the University of Marburg. He has held positions at the University of Hamburg, SIBA, and Dharma Drum Institute.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a B.A. from Brooklyn College and a Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of the Buddhist Association of the United States (2013).

Bhikkhu Pāsādika works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at Magadh and Punjabi Universities, he taught at Punjabi University (1975–1977), worked at the Göttingen Academy (1980–1993), and served as president of Linh Son Buddhist Academy (2016).
Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) under the doctoral supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe.

Bhogilal Sandesara was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served as Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1951–1975) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (~1958–1975).

Bhuwan Lal Joshi was a scholar of Indology who studied at Patna University. He worked at the University of California, Berkeley (~1962–1967) and served as a professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz (~1967–1977).

Bidia Dandaron was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg institutions, learning under Andrei Vostrikov, and held research posts at the Buryat Institute of Social Sciences (1956) and the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies (1957).

Bihani Sarkar is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She held a post at the University of Hamburg and is attested in 2026 as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University.

Bill M. Mak is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He served as Associate Professor at Kyoto University (2014–2019) and became a Professor at the University of Science and Technology of China in 2024, holding research fellowships at NRI and the University of Hamburg.

Bimal Krishna Matilal was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as Professor at the University of Toronto (~1968–1976) and Spalding Professor at Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of London under Lionel David Barnett. He served as Head of Department at Patna University (1958) and Honorary Joint Director of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1969–1977).
